analysis.title: GS US TMT .. bounce back (Peter Callahan, TMT Sector Specialist, 15 Nov 2026)
key_insights: NDX broke a 4-week losing streak, closing up ~350 bps on the week. Semis/SOX rose ~800 bps, the best week since early August. Both NDX and SOX still closed below their 200-dmas on Friday.
Last week's headlines around NVDA drove two-way debate. Strength showed in AMD and the ASICs ecosystem. NVDA is down 12% YTD after its biggest week of underperformance relative to Semis since 2008.
US Financial Conditions rose to their tightest level in ~18 months after another hotter CPI print. 10yr yields are back at 5.15% and oil is back towards $96/brl.

Callahan attributes the bounce mostly to cleaner positioning (GS PB data showed covering via macro products) and intra-market rotations into Defensives, Big Tech (including AMD and AVGO) and Low Vol names, including Pharma. This created debate about how much room is left to run.

Callahan sees relatively little consensus in the market for the first time in a while, apart from a broadly receptive tilt towards Hyperscalers. Debate centers on where we are in the AI/Semi cycle, what is priced in, and whether this is a bear market bounce or a bull market forming.
Software dispersion has picked up, including within Cyber and Data Infra. Internet has become squeezy and hard to trade, though some 'value' interest is emerging.

Callahan describes consensus positioning and sentiment as a 'blank slate' on how to trade the AI cycle. Options raised: buy quality or stable-GM semis, buy the dip in higher-octane areas (EMS, Memory, Neos), rotate into hyperscalers, or look for cross-sector inconsistencies. He calls this arguably a healthier investing landscape into 2027.

Top client inbounds last week: why the bounce in Tech/AI and whether it is sustainable, memory stack rankings (HDDs, DRAM, NAND), whether people are long or short AI/Semis, interest in 'new' Internet ideas (OTAs, UBER, NFLX, APP), the set-up into the NVDA print, why AMAT and CSCO fell so much T+1, and META vs MSFT.

NVDA market cap is back below $4trn and now matches MSFT's. MDB, MSFT, DELL and TSM are testing their 50-dma to the downside. ZS is lower on 12 of 14 days. EBAY and ETSY are up 6 of 7 weeks. Staples, Low Vol and Pharma continue to move sharply higher. CMCSA and CHTR are 20-35% off their lows.

GS Macro Outlook for 2027: global growth of 2.8%, as lower energy prices and strong AI capex outweigh tighter financial conditions and more neutral fiscal policy. Risks are tilted to the downside: renewed Iran escalation, large fiscal deficits pushing up long-term yields (especially France), and AI capex disappointment. GS also sees early signs of AI weighing on the job market.

NVDA reports Tuesday 11/17 post close. The stock has a 14-day RSI of 24, the lowest since 2019, and trades at 11x NTM P/E. Investor focus is on Vera Rubin momentum, visibility into 2027+, gross margins and capital allocation.

DIS reports Tuesday 11/17 pre-market. The stock is re-testing the $120s level that has acted as a ceiling for ~4+ years. Focus is on strategic initiatives into 2027+ (cruise fleet expansion, park capex, theatrical pipeline, Disney+ integration of merchandise and interactive features planned for Spring 2027).

PANW reports Wednesday 11/18 post close. The stock fell on T+1 in 9 of the last 12 prints, is in the low ~$300s and about $100 off its YTD highs. Sentiment is upbeat as it is seen as a thematically 'right way' AI name. Focus is on AI uplift as it laps the CyberArk and Chronosphere acquisitions in 1Q'C27.

INTU reports Thursday 11/19 post close. Inbounds are very low and the stock has not closed above its 200-dma in more than a year. It is a 'show me' story, with focus on Intuit Intelligence, QuickBooks industry verticals and broader Consumer touchpoints.

AAPL vs NDX is approaching highs. Investors are frustrated that bear points after Apple's recent earnings (Services deceleration, GM headwinds, AI unknowns around server-side inference costs) have not weighed on the stock.
SPX ex-AI has outperformed SPX over the last year and was more resilient in last week's sell-off (per L Miller).

sector_views.rationale: SOX rose ~800 bps on the week but remains below its 200-dma. Callahan sees no consensus on the AI/Semi cycle and lists quality semis, higher-octane areas and hyperscalers as competing ways to trade it.

Dispersion has picked up, including within Cyber and Data Infra. Several software charts look better than the theme suggests (PCOR, PCTY, FROG, DOCU, BOX, MANH), though Callahan says there is no real theme.
The group has become squeezy and difficult to trade. Some 'value' interest is emerging, and clients are asking about OTAs, UBER, NFLX and APP.
